  “(California Government Code Section 54954.3).
  (a) Every agenda for regular meetings shall provide an opportunity for members of the
  public to directly address the legislative body on any item of interest to the public, before
  or during the legislative body’s consideration of the item, that is within the subject matter
  jurisdiction of the legislative body, provided that no action shall be taken on any item not
  appearing on the agenda unless the action is otherwise authorized by subdivision (b) of
  Section 54954.2 [section omitted].

  (b) (1) The legislative body of a local agency may adopt reasonable regulations to ensure
  that the intent of the subdivision (a) is carried out, including, but not limited to, regulations
  limiting the total amount of time allocated for public testimony on particular issues and for
  each individual speaker.
  (2) Notwithstanding paragraph (1), when the legislative body of a local agency limits
  time for public comment, the legislative body of a local agency shall provide at least twice
  the allotted time to a member of the public who utilizes a translator to ensure that non-
  English speakers receive the same opportunity to directly address the legislative body of
  a local agency.”

  In furtherance of Section 54954.3 of the Brown Act, the public is allotted to speak a total
  of three (3) minutes on the entirety of the Consent Calendar, Appointment(s), New

  desired, an additional two (2) minutes on items not on the agenda that are within the
  subject matter jurisdiction of the City Council. As specified in the Brown Act, a speaker
  utilizing a translator will receive twice the amount of time specified.

SUBJECT:  ADOPT RESOLUTION NO. CC 2023-042 A RESOLUTION OF THE
  CITY COUNCIL OF THE CITY OF PALMDALE ESTABLISHING AN
  APPROPRIATIONS LIMIT FOR FISCAL YEAR 2023-24 PURSUANT
  TO ARTICLE XIII B OF THE CALIFORNIA CONSTITUTION AND
  REPEAL RESOLUTION NO. CC 2022-067

ISSUE
Adopt Resolution No. CC 2023-042 a Resolution of the City Council of the City of
Palmdale establishing an appropriations limit for Fiscal Year 2023-24 pursuant to Article
XIII B of the California Constitution and repeal Resolution No. CC 2022-067.

RECOMMENDATION
Staff recommends that the City Council adopt Resolution No. CC 2023-042 to establish
a new appropriations limit for Fiscal Year 2023-24 pursuant to Article XIII B of the
Constitution of the State of California and repeal Resolution No. CC 2022-067.

BACKGROUND
Article XIIIB of the California State Constitution, more commonly referred to as the Gann
Initiative or Gann Appropriations Limit, was adopted by California voters in 1980. The
Gann Appropriations Limit places restrictions on the amount of tax proceeds that state
and local governmental agencies can receive and appropriate each fiscal year.

The Limit changes each fiscal year and is different for each governmental agency. The
Limit is calculated based on the actual amount of tax proceeds appropriated during the
1978-79 fiscal year and is increased each year for inflation and population growth.
Inflationary adjustments are, by law, based on the growth in the California Per Capita
Income or the growth in non-residential assessed valuation due to new construction within
the City. Population adjustments are based on the population growth of the City or the
population growth within the City's county. The decision as to which of the options to
select is made annually by a recorded vote of the City Council.

The statutes regarding the adoption of the Appropriations Limit, contained in
Government Code Section 7910, require the governing body to annually adopt, by
resolution, an appropriations limit each year for the following fiscal year.
 Report to Mayor and City Council
Re: Adopt Resolution No. CC 2023-042 Establishing Appropriations Limit for FY 2023-
24
June 21, 2023
Page 2

DISCUSSION
For fiscal year 2023-24, the City of Palmdale estimates that tax proceeds to be received,
as well as tax proceeds appropriated by the City Council, will, as in prior years, continue
to be under the legal limit. The City's appropriations limit for fiscal year 2023-24 is
established at $165,259,617, a 3.75 percent increase over the fiscal year 2022-23 limit.
This is the maximum amount of tax proceeds the City will be able to receive and
appropriate in the coming fiscal year. The City's appropriations subject to the limit for
fiscal year 2023-24 are estimated to be $98,357,495. Therefore, the City's fiscal year
2023-24 adopted budget appropriations subject to the limit are $66,902,122 less than
the appropriations limit.

FISCAL IMPACT
There is no direct fiscal impact as a result of this action. Resolution No. CC 2023-042
would increase the total annual appropriations limit from $159,286,378 to
$165,259,617.

   CITY COUNCIL
  CITY OF PALMDALE, CALIFORNIA
  RESOLUTION NO. CC 2023-042

  A RESOLUTION OF THE CITY COUNCIL OF THE CITY OF PALMDALE
  ESTABLISHING AN APPROPRIATIONS LIMIT FOR FY 2023-24
  PURSUANT TO ARTICLE XIII B OF THE CALIFORNIA CONSTITUTION
  AND REPEAL RESOLUTION NO. CC 2022-067.

  WHEREAS, Article XIII B of the California Constitution provides that the total
annual appropriations subject to limitation for each governmental entity, including this
City, shall not exceed the appropriations limit of such entity of government for the prior
year, as adjusted for changes in the California per capita income or assessment roll for
new non-residential construction and population, except as otherwise provided for in
said Article XIII B and implementing State statutes; and

  WHEREAS, pursuant to said Article XIII B of the California Constitution, and
Section 7910 of the California Government Code, the City is required to establish its
appropriations limit each year for the following fiscal year; and

  WHEREAS, since the data necessary to calculate the increase in the non-
residential assessed valuation is generally not available from County assessors, there
is the possible need to adjust the limit once the assessment data is available; and

  WHEREAS, the City Manager has caused the limit for the City of Palmdale to be
calculated and determined, on a provisional basis, using the per capita income and City
population factors, and said appropriations limit for the fiscal year 2023-24 has been,
and is hereby provisionally established in the amount of $165,259,617; and

  WHEREAS, the documentation and calculations necessary to arrive at said
limitation amount have heretofore been available for public inspection for the required
fifteen (15) days.

NOW THEREFORE, BE IT RESOLVED, THE CITY COUNCIL OF THE CITY OF
PALMDALE DOES HEREBY FIND, DETERMINE, RESOLVE AND ORDER AS
FOLLOWS:

  SECTION 1. Adopt Resolution No. CC 2023-042 establishing an appropriation
limit in the amount of $165,259,617 for Fiscal Year 2023-24; and

Staff recommends that the City Council:

  exceed $205,000.
Adoption of this Purchase Order is contingent upon the City Council approving
the FY 2023-24 City of Palmdale Annual Budget.

BACKGROUND
The City established an Amazon Business Prime account through a cooperative
purchasing agreement through OMNIA Partners, Public Sector Contract No. R-TC-
17006 with Amazon Capital Services to procure Office & Operating Supplies, Program
Supplies, Equipment, Technology Equipment, and Furniture. The use of Cooperative
Purchasing is authorized in Palmdale Municipal Code §3.08.140 (D) for the City to
participate with other public agencies and/or with non-profit groups or organizations for
the purpose of cooperative purchasing. Cooperative purchasing is a fiscally responsible
approach for the City to streamline the purchasing process saving time and resources
that would have been spent on preparing and conducting formal Invitation for Bids for a
myriad of products. Besides reducing administrative costs, the City is already a member

additional savings through competitive pricing.

DISCUSSION

Amazon Capital Services, Inc. dba Amazon Business to procure Office & Operating
Supplies, Program Supplies, Equipment, Technology Equipment, and Furniture, in an
amount not to exceed $205,000.00 for FY 2023-24.

FISCAL IMPACT

$205,000.00. Funds for this Purchase Order and all other expenditures with Amazon
Capital Services are currently budgeted in Office, Operating, Program Supplies,
Equipment & Furniture less than $5K, and General City Accounts.

STRATEGIC PLAN

Goal II: Ensure long-term fiscal health of the City and maintain funding for services.
  A. Manage resources, costs, and liabilities to ensure the City’s long-term fiscal
  health.

BACKGROUND
The City’s Classification and Pay Plans are a component of its budget. Later this evening
the City Council will vote on whether or not to adopt the FY 2023 - 2024 City of Palmdale
budget. Adoption of this Resolution is contingent upon the City Council approving
the FY 2023 - 2024 City of Palmdale budget.

DISCUSSION
The California Public Employees’ Retirement System (CalPERS) requires the City to
approve Classification and Pay Plans separately, not in combination with other items on
the agenda, such as the budget. To comply with CalPERS guidelines, the staff is
submitting the City’s Classification and Pay Plans for approval.

Staff recommends the City Council adopt Resolution Nos. CC 2023-044, CC 2023-045,
and CC 2023-046 amending the City’s Classification and Pay Plans.

FISCAL IMPACT
Funds are budgeted in the FY 2023 - 2024 budget and no further allocation of funds is
required by the City Council.

ISSUE
Approve authorizing City Manager to bind insurance coverages related to the agreement
between VINSA, Inc. and City of Palmdale (A-7994) in an amount not to exceed
$2,750,000.

RECOMMENDATION
Staff recommends that the City Council:
  1. Authorize the City Manager or her designee to bind insurance coverages in a total
  amount not to exceed $2,750,000 for fiscal year 2023-2024.

BACKGROUND
VINSA has been the City’s insurance broker for almost three decades and is currently
under agreement until September 30, 2027. The company was incorporated in 1986 and
has serviced thousands of Antelope Valley residents, corporations and public entities.
VINSA has had an exceptional record while working for the City, including keeping costs
contained, reviewing coverages and negotiating with nationwide insurance companies
and self-insured pools specializing in public entities.

Staff proposes that the City Council authorize the City Manager to bind insurance
coverage according to the agreement between VINSA, Inc. and the City of Palmdale (A-
7994).

VINSA has already provided quotes to staff for the following types of coverage: liability,
property, the difference in conditions, employment practices, public officials bonds, crime
liability, volunteer liability, special events coverage and any other insurance programs
agreed upon by both parties.

between VINSA, Inc. and City of Palmdale (A-7994)

DISCUSSION

Staff requests that the Council authorize the City Manager to bind coverage for the City
and its related entities. This will ensure there is no lapse in coverage. The Policy
Schedule shows the current estimated insurance coverage and costs, but the final costs
may be adjusted, depending on market conditions and whether staff decides to increase
or decrease coverage, or coverage types, based upon market conditions.

FISCAL IMPACT
Funds for this agreement are budgeted in the following account:
  A. 15014101-711000 (Insurance premiums - liability)
  B. 15014101-711004 (Insurance – worker’s comp – volunteers)
Although the contract does not specify an exact amount, we anticipate the fiscal impact
for Fiscal Year 2023 – 2024 will not exceed $2,750,000.00 (inclusive of VINSA’s broker
fees and commissions). Approximately $250,000 represents VINSA’s broker fee of 10%
of net insurance purchased (i.e., excluding costs) and/or commissions. The remaining
amount represents payments to the insurance companies for the various coverages.
Payments may vary depending on multiple factors such as the insurance market, actuarial
history, number of participants in the self-insured pool, increase in City assets and the
need to purchase additional policies, among other things.

ISSUE
Adopt Resolution No. CC 2023-043 a Resolution of the City Council of the City of
Palmdale restating in its entirety the City of Palmdale Master Schedule of Fees and
Repealing all prior enactments inconsistent with this Resolution.

RECOMMENDATION
Staff recommends that the City Council:

  1. Adopt Resolution No. CC 2023-043 to authorize the proposed fees and charges
  for the fees, charges, and requirements set forth in the City of Palmdale Master
  Schedule of Fees for Service, effective July 1, 2023, and attached hereto; and,

  2. Repeal all prior enactments inconsistent with Resolution No. CC 2022-043.

BACKGROUND
The State Constitution provides the authority for cities to impose user fees and
regulatory fees for services and activities, however the fees may not exceed the
estimated reasonable cost of providing the service or performing the activity.

Periodically, the City Council adopts Fee Resolutions, which 1) revise existing fees,
rates, or charges; 2) establish new fees, rates, or charges; or 3) revise headings or
descriptive language for existing fees for the City's operating departments. Fee
adjustments are necessary to keep pace with inflation and recover costs.

The last citywide fee schedule, adopted on June 29, 2022, did not include increases to
City imposed fees. However, it incorporated policy updates and minor revisions to the
Fee Schedules.
 Report to Mayor and City Council
Re: Adopt Resolution No. CC 2023-043 Restating in its Entirety the Palmdale Fee
Schedule and Repealing all prior enactments inconsistent with this Resolution
June 21, 2023
Page 2

DISCUSSION
To better achieve the City’s policy regarding cost recovery goals and to minimize
General Fund subsidies for services provided, staff proposes adjustments to the Fee
Schedule as outlined in the attached City of Palmdale Master Schedule of Fees.

The U.S. Bureau of Labor Statistics publishes the Consumer Price Index (CPI) monthly,
which compares the current prices for consumer goods to the prices one year ago. The
Consumer Price Index for the period of April 2022 to April 2023 measured an increase
in the price of overall goods of 3.8%. The proposed fee schedule incorporates an
increase to all City imposed fees based on the CPI for the Greater Los Angeles area
from April 2022 to April 2023, of 3.8%. Adjusting by the CPI allows the City to increase
fees gradually to offset expenditure increases better, and to avoid drastic measures in
future years.

Any action by the City to levy a new fee or service charge or to approve an increase in
an existing fee or service must be approved by ordinance or resolution. Before any new
fee or service charge can be added to the City of Palmdale Master Schedule of Fees, a
public hearing must be held, and reasonable notice must be provided to the community
members.

As such, Staff recommends that the City Council Adopt Resolution No. CC 2023-043
and Repeal Resolution Nos. CC 2022-065, 2022-091 and 2023-013, authorizing the
proposed adjustments to the City of Palmdale Master Schedule of Fees, effective July
1, 2023.

PUBLIC NOTICE PROCESS
A Public Hearing Notice regarding the citywide fee resolution was published in the local
newspaper of general circulation on June 6, 2023, June 13, 2023, and June 20, 2023,
at which time the public was invited to make oral and written presentation as part of the
regularly scheduled meeting prior to the adoption of Resolution No. CC 2023-043.
Additionally, written notice has been provided to interested parties, who filed written
requests for mailed notice of meeting on new or increased development related fees or
service charges, at least 14 days prior to the public meeting.

FISCAL IMPACT
Resolution No. CC 2023-043, if adopted, would allow certain fees to be adjusted and
policies to be enacted, which will allow the City to better recoup costs and continue
providing services to the community.

  3. The City Council finds that providing these Services is of special benefit to

  desires to better recover the costs of providing these Services from

Definitions:
1. Agencies with proof of Internal Revenue Code IRC 501 (c) (3) (4) (5) and (6) are considered non-profits.
2. Commercial use is defined as an event held for the purpose of generating monetary gain for the event sponsor(s).
3. Direct program costs are exclusively incurred as a result of the program and are frequently variable, adjusting as program participation
  varies. Direct cost examples include part-time personnel, supplies, contract services and equipment. DryTown direct costs include the
  preceding expenses in addition to: full-time salaries, park utilities and equipment.
4. Indirect program costs that are shared among several programs and are necessary to execute general day-to-day operations. Indirect
  cost examples include personnel overhead, utilities and custodial expenses. Indirect costs are not considered as fees and charges
  are determined.
Policies
1. Non-profit with verifiable status of IRC 501 (c) (3) (4) (5) or (6) are eligible for a 25% facility reservation rate reduction. Unless otherwise
  specified, facility reservation fees that are eligible for a rate reduction are noted by an *. Rate reductions do not apply to personnel fees,
  facility deposits or equipment rental. Similarly, program fees for non-residents will increase 25% and DryTown admission fees for
  non-residents will increase 15%. Services subject to non-resident increase are noted by an **.
2. Unless otherwise specified, the rate for use of facilities for commercial purposes shall be charged at 200% of the hourly reservation fee,
  in addition to 5% gross admission ticket sales and gross alcohol sales. These fees may be reduced or waived if the applicant can
  demonstrate that residents of the City of Palmdale benefit from the use of facilities or the services being provided.
3. Unless otherwise specified, set-up and clean-up charges are comprised of applicable facility hourly reservation rates.
4. Park parking lots are generally not available for exclusive use reservations. If exclusivity can be accommodated and if parking fees are
  charged by the renter, 25% of parking fees collected are to be paid to the City.
5. Parks & Recreation program and service fees are established by following specified cost recovery policies. Fees and charges are
  determined by identifying direct costs if providing services and apply the cost recovery goals stated below. Direct program costs are
  referenced in the definitions section. It is widely accepted that park and recreation systems are publicly financed, and therefore offer free
  or affordable services. The level of program subsidy will be based on an assessment of the community or social benefit, local market and
  economic conditions. As services have a greater appeal to individuals or groups of individuals, it is appropriate to charge fees for the
  services at an increasing rate of cost recovery. Cost recovery target categories include: Community Benefit/Access, free; Community
  Benefit, 0-25%; Balanced Beneficiaries, 25-50%; Substantial Individual Benefit, 50-75%; Exclusive Individual Benefit, 75-100%.
  Cost recovery categories are further defined in Exhibit L-1.
General Fees
1. Unless otherwise specified, a special event application processing fee of $250 may be charged for staff services required to process the
  application, which may include coordination with other City departments, or State and County government agencies. The fee is
  non-refundable and does not guarantee approval of the application.
2. Unless otherwise specified, fees for personnel shall be calculated at hourly rate for staff wages, plus 45% for full-time benefits or 15%
  for part-time benefits and a 25% administrative fee. Unless the use warrants otherwise, staff will be scheduled to be on-site
  one-half hour before and after use. All personnel charges are a two-hour minimum.

BACKGROUND
Each year the City is required to adopt a budget for the operation of the City. The budget
serves as the City’s financial plan for the Fiscal Year beginning July 1 through June 30.
It defines City priorities for the provision of services to the community.

According to the Palmdale Municipal Code: Chapter 3.04 Budget Adoption Procedures,
the City Manager shall submit a proposed budget to the City Council no later than May
31st of each year. The proposed budget was brought before the City Council on May
17, 2023. Additionally, the City Council shall conduct a public hearing on the proposed
budget before adoption and shall adopt a budget prescribing the spending policy of the
City for the ensuing fiscal year on or before the thirtieth day of June of each year.

DISCUSSION
Staff is bringing forth the Proposed Budget for Fiscal Year 2023-24 for your review and
consideration.
March 10, 2023, the City Council held a retreat, focusing on goal setting for the upcoming
year. In alignment with those goals, staff have developed the proposed FY 2024 budget
for consideration.
City Council’s goals and priorities include:
    Building Culture & Community
    Economic Vitality and Innovation
    Social Unity
    Transportation and Infrastructure
The Citywide budget represents all funds within the City, including the General Fund,
Measure AV Fund, Special Revenue, Enterprise, Debt Service and Capital Funds.

Revenues
Estimating revenues for the upcoming fiscal year and forecasting out-years is essential
to the budget development process. Revenue projections are formed by analyzing
prior year actual receipts, trends, new revenue sources, grant opportunities, fees for
services, and State economic outlook. Citywide revenues are estimated to be $476.1
million.
The City’s General Fund is the largest unrestricted funding source with a total of
$101.8 million in projected resources. General Fund resources include property tax,
sales tax, other taxes, fees, and charges for service. Measure AV is a general sales
and use tax that, although not required, the City presents separate from the General
Fund for transparency purposes. Measure AV has a total of $22.9 million in projected
resources projected in Fiscal Year 2023-24.

Conclusion

maintaining healthy reserves. The proposed FY 2023-24 Budget is balanced and
represents the City’s commitment to the long-term planning and sustainability of
programs and services for the community.

The Fiscal Year 2023-24 Operating Budget will serve as the financial guideline for
program implementation for the year. The proposed annual budget is compliant with all
Financial Policies, including the 20% General Fund Reserve Requirement, with a 30%
reserve proposed in the budget. It is anticipated that revenues will be sufficient to cover
the expenditures proposed.

SUBJECT:  CITY COUNCIL NOMINATION AND APPOINTMENT OF ONE (1)

ISSUE
City Council Nomination and Appointment of one (1) Member to the Board of Library
Trustees.

RECOMMENDATION
Staff recommends that City Council nominate and appoint one (1) member to serve on
the Board of Library Trustees. While it is preferable that a City Councilmember’s
appointee reside within the Councilmember’s district, it is not required. The District
information is being provided for information only. City Clerk received two (2)
applications, both applicants reside in District 2:
  1. Challen David
  2. Delilah Harris

BACKGROUND
The Library Board is made up of five (5) members, who are nominated and appointed
according to PMC Section 2.08.030. The Board of Library Trustees operates under the
Education Code, serve a three-year term, and must be a resident of the City of
Palmdale.

DISCUSSION
The term for Challen David, Board of Library Trustees, will expire June 30, 2023. A
recruitment advertisement was placed in the AV Press for interested citizens to apply.
The Communications Division also provided a press release to the public, including the
application submittal deadline, and posted the advertisement on the City’s Social Media
platforms. The Classified Ad and the application were made available on the Current
Vacancies webpage and the Board of Library Trustees webpage, as well as in the
Office of the City Clerk. Staff received two (2) applications.
 Report to Mayor and City Council
Re: Board of Library Trustee Appointment
June 21, 2023
Page 2

Appointments to the Board of Library Trustees are made according to PMC 2.08.030
(C) & (D) which states the following:

  (C) All such applications shall be provided to the City Council for review, who
  shall, at a regularly scheduled City Council meeting, nominate, from among such
  applicants, the persons whom the City Councilmembers desire to appoint by
  making a motion for each such appointment.

  (D) If the nomination is approved by a majority vote of the City Council, the
  nominating City Councilmember may then proceed to appoint the person to the
  board or commission under consideration.

This item is brought forth for City Council Nomination and Appointment of one (1)
Member for a term to expire June 2026.

A Livescan fingerprint submission via the California Department of Justice is required
for the appointment to be complete. The State of California requires a Statement of
Economic Interest Form 700 be filed within 30-days of the appointment.

FISCAL IMPACT
Approximately $1,061 in advertising cost. The Chair is compensated $150 per meeting,
a maximum of $300 per month, and all other Members $100 per meeting, a maximum of
$200 per month.
